explainer_content.short_definition: 1990s roots rock that keeps country twang but distrusts country-radio gloss.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Alt-country emerged from bands and writers who loved country and folk traditions but carried indie-rock habits, rougher guitars, and anti-commercial posture.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It helped build the modern Americana conversation and gave roots music a college-rock and club-scene pathway.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The twang sounds deliberately scuffed, with rock-band edges and songwriter melancholy in the foreground.

canonical_example_rationales.why_this_example_matters: Son Volt anchors Alt-country and No Depression by making story-first lyrics and twang or pedal-steel color easier to hear.
Uncle Tupelo anchors Alt-country and No Depression by making twang or pedal-steel color and dance or ballad pacing easier to hear.
Trace - Son Volt anchors Alt-country and No Depression by making dance or ballad pacing and plainspoken vocal stance easier to hear.
Strangers Almanac - Whiskeytown anchors Alt-country and No Depression by making plainspoken vocal stance and radio polish against roots texture easier to hear.
No Depression - Uncle Tupelo anchors Alt-country and No Depression by making radio polish against roots texture and story-first lyrics easier to hear.
Windfall - Son Volt anchors Alt-country and No Depression by making story-first lyrics and twang or pedal-steel color easier to hear.
